standard_prerequisites.name: Inconsistency via closed tableaux
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set of sentences is inconsistent iff some finite subset has a closed tableau; the witnesses are closed tableaux for finite signed assumption sets built from the set.
standard_prerequisites.use: Inconsistency of Gamma union {A} is unpacked into a finite witness C_1,...,C_m from Gamma with a closed tableau carrying True A among its assumptions.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Cut rule
standard_prerequisites.statement: A tableau branch may be split on any sentence A into a branch with True A and one with False A.
standard_prerequisites.use: The two closed witnesses are combined into one closed tableau by a single Cut application on A.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 902-905): if Gamma proves A and Gamma union {A} is inconsistent, then Gamma is inconsistent.

Witness extraction (proof lines 908-915): finite Gamma_0 = {B_1,...,B_n} and Gamma_1 = {C_1,...,C_m} subsets of Gamma such that {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n} and {True A, True C_1,...,True C_m} both have closed tableaux; the first is the unpacking of Gamma proves A, the second of the inconsistency of Gamma union {A}.

Cut combination (proof lines 916-920): the Cut rule on A merges the two closed tableaux into a single closed tableau showing Gamma_0 union Gamma_1 is inconsistent; since Gamma_0 and Gamma_1 are both subsets of Gamma, so is their union, hence Gamma is inconsistent.
proof_roadmap: Unpack both hypotheses into finite closed-tableau witnesses over Gamma.
Apply the Cut rule on A to merge the two witnesses into one closed tableau.
Conclude by finite-subset monotonicity that Gamma itself is inconsistent.
difficulty_reason: Contrapositive closure (statement 902-905, proof 907-921): the complete Cut-combination argument, including both witness unpackings and the subset step, carried in prose in span. H2.
